items.title: Dave Liebman — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: he is definitely my first jazz mentor, no question about it

ctx.x: doctrinaire is the word. For whatever, he wouldn’t be a sideman. He wouldn’t do anything. He was only going to be a bandleader and didn’t meet with success. I don’t know what happened. He became a lawyer. He became – in some things, he was my lawyer over these next – what? – 30, 40 years, until he retired. Very frustrating, but, to finish this part of the story, he is definitely my first jazz mentor, no question about it, outside of friends and things we’ve been discussing, peers or older peers. He’s the first…
You know his one Blue Note album, right? Basra.
Oh, yeah. Of course. We played Turkish with him, Turkish Women at the Bath, and we played Eider Down. We played those tunes. He was some musician.
